$comment: Regression floors for `python3 eval/harness.py --gate`, compared at three decimals — the precision they are stated at and the scorecard is rendered at. Set to the values actually measured on 2026-08-12, not to round numbers below them: Tier 0 is fully deterministic — same code, same corpus, same result — so there is no run-to-run variance for a margin to absorb, and a floor below the measured value is just permission to regress silently. Raise these when a real improvement lands; lowering one needs a written reason in the PR, because the whole point of a gate you can edit is that editing it is visible.
$comment_min_recall: 60 of 61 labelled vulnerabilities across 15 languages. The single miss is V3 (IDOR / broken access control), which has no reliable static signature and is documented as belonging to the LLM tier — see kit/tests/test_engine.py. If this floor ever needs lowering, the honest move is to state which class stopped being detected. Note that a rising overall figure can still hide a class going dark, which is why --gate also fails on any previously-detected class, CWE or language dropping to zero.
$comment_min_f3: F3 weights recall 9x over precision, which is RealVuln's primary metric and the right shape for a security scanner: a missed vulnerability costs more than a triaged false alarm. Measured 0.985.
$comment_max_trap_false_positives: A false positive here is a hit on a SAFE implementation of the same feature as its vulnerable twin — the hardest trap in the corpus and the one that decides whether people keep reading our reports. Zero is not aspirational; it is the measured value, and it must stay measured.

measured.$comment: The run these floors were derived from. eval/scorecard.md is the full breakdown and CI fails if it drifts from what the engine currently measures.
